messages:
Aisha (marketing): Quick request for eng/runtime folks — were finalizing webinar & landing page benchmarks. Can someone own a clean rerun + sanity checks for the numbers under s3://redwood-marketing/bench-q2/ ? Need raw logs, a short summary, and a small CSV aggregated for marketing by Friday EOD.

Aisha (marketing): Must-haves: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, 95th mem usage, run_id, commit hash, driver + CUDA, and links to artifacts. Flag any non-representative tests.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Ill take this. Couple clarifying q's: which model variants (fp16, q4)? exact seq lengths & batch sizes? Cold vs warm caching?

Aisha (marketing): Models: gpt-redwood-7b (fp16) and gpt-redwood-7b-q4_0 (int8). Seq lengths: 64, 256, 1024. Batches: 1, 4. Please produce cold-start (no cached KV) and warm-start (prefix cache enabled) runs. Use prompts at s3://redwood-marketing/bench-q2/inputs/list.txt.

Marta (eng-ml): Methodology notes: use identical RNG seed across repeats, 100 warmup iters + 400 measured, clear KV between cold requests, measure tokens/sec in measured window only, report model load time separately, and include kernel fallback counts if available.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Running on our p4d test pool (CUDA 12.1, driver 535). Will use release/v2.3 commit hash unless you want a different one. Will not tune microkernels — use default shipping config per request.

Aisha (marketing): That release/v2.3 hash is fine. Important: marketing wants numbers that reflect default customer experience. No special perf hacks.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Started runs. Command used: 
```
./bin/bench_runner \
  --model gpt-redwood-7b \
  --quant fp16 \
  --seq 64,256,1024 \
  --batch 1,4 \
  --warmup 100 \
  --measure 400 \
  --clear-kv true \
  --seed 1234 \
  --out s3://redwood-marketing/bench-q2/runs/1750123456/
```
Also ran q4 variant similarly. Posting run ids when available.

BenchmarkBot (bot): Registered run_id=run-20240305-2a7c, artifacts: s3://redwood-marketing/bench-q2/runs/run-20240305-2a7c/, status: started

Kevin (eng-runtime): Preliminary summary (fp16): seq=64,batch=1 -> p50=12ms, p95=28ms, p99=56ms, tokens/sec=1200, mem~12.1GB. seq=1024 shows p99 outliers at ~420ms on ~0.5% requests; saw attention kernel fallback. Will run focused longer test for seq=1024 to reduce noise.

Marta (eng-ml): Please compute delta vs golden baseline run_id=run-20240115-golden and include percent change. For statistical comparability, include simple 95% CI on tokens/sec or note if variance is high.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Will do. Scheduling a rerun for seq=1024 with 2000 measured iters: run_id=run-20240305-2a7c-rerun1.

BenchmarkBot (bot): Rerun completed  run_id=run-20240305-2a7c-rerun1  artifacts uploaded

BenchmarkBot (bot): Artifact summary CSVs present. Quick diff vs golden: fp16 p50 -2.8% faster, p95 -0.8% faster, p99 +5.1% (regression on long seq). q4 int8: tokens/sec +10.3% vs fp16, mem -3.9%, p99 variance higher. Full CSV and logs in artifacts.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Findings: p99 regression at seq=1024 caused by kernel fallback for certain attention sizes; p95 remains stable and representative. Recommendation for marketing: lead with p95 numbers and include a footnote about rare p99 spikes on long sequences with link to raw logs. I can also produce a single-row marketing CSV (one line per model/seq/batch) if helpful.

Sam (marketing): Please add that CSV to the run folder. Also recommend the one-line headline: do we use p50 or p95?

Oliver (product): Use p95 for headline — more stable for user-facing claims. Keep raw logs linked for audit.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Draft one-liner for marketing: "On release/v2.3, gpt-redwood-7b (fp16) achieves p95 latency of 28ms for 64-token responses on p4d; q4 int8 boosts tokens/sec by ~10% while lowering memory by ~4% (run_id=run-20240305-2a7c)."

Aisha (marketing): Great. Thats exactly what I need. Sam, Ill hand off the CSV and one-liner to you for copy. Leaving artifacts in S3 and keeping run readme with exact commands.

Kevin (eng-runtime): CSV added: s3://redwood-marketing/bench-q2/runs/run-20240305-2a7c/marketing_summary.csv. README with methodology and exact commands is present. If marketing wants an annotated slide with the p95/p99 explanation I can help draft it.

Marta (eng-ml): Side note: if we later change kernel selection to optimize long-seq paths, we should retest p99 before any major claims.

Aisha (marketing): Will include that footnote and hold any major comparative claims until kernel work is complete. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
